guidelines.detail: documentation rule FID-01 not applied (S2 states that the R&D team conducts initial research and feasibility studies, then drafts design concepts. The generated model has no counterpart for the feasibility-study task (M7), so one stated activity was dropped. The start-event mismatch (M13, X1) is a separate issue that LRN-005 and LRN-010 already cover, so this proposal targets the dropped activity instead.)

refines FID-02 (The description states three distinct evaluations of the prototype in one sentence, but the generated model combined them into one task labelled with all three. The reference models each evaluation as its own task (M3, M4, M6), and the generated task X2 has no counterpart. Modeling each evaluation as a separate task in stated order removes this divergence. The wording avoids this process's domain )

refines EVT-02 (The reference models the two closing outcomes as tasks (an approval task and a discard task) after the outcome gateway, each followed by an end event. The generated model goes straight from the gateway to two end events, so the performed actions are missing (M1, M3) and the end events carry the outcomes instead (X2, X3). The documented guideline EVT-02 only says to use end events for terminal outc)

refines EVT-01 (The reference models identifying the idea, approving the prototype and discarding it as tasks. The generated model instead turned the identification into the label of a start event and the approval and discard outcomes into labels of end events, so the three tasks are missing and two end events and one start event have no counterpart. The description (S1, S7) states these as actions the process pe)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says one actor carries out several consecutive actions before a later creative step, such as an initial research activity, then a feasibility study, then drafting concepts

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several distinct evaluations of the same artifact in one sentence, separated by commas or 'and': Model each listed evaluation as its own task, in the order the description states them, and connect the tasks in sequence. Do not combine them into one task whose label lists all the evaluations. Place any outcome that the description attaches to the evaluations after the last task of the sequence.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several distinct evaluations of the same artifact in one sentence, separated by commas or 'and'

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the case ends with one of two alternative outcomes chosen at a decision point, where each outcome is stated as an action taken on the item (for example the item is taken forward or it is dropped): Model the decision as an exclusive gateway placed after the preceding evaluation step. Give each outcome its own task, named for the action performed on the item, and connect that task to the gateway by a sequence flow. Connect each outcome task to its own end event by a sequence flow. Do not connect the gateway directly to the end events, and do not use the end event label to carry the outcome action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the case ends with one of two alternative outcomes chosen at a decision point, where each outcome is stated as an action taken on the item (for example the item is taken forward or it is dropped)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a performed work action at the very beginning or the very end of the process (for example, an identification step that opens the process, or one of several approval or rejection actions that closes it), and that action is described as something done rather than as a message or condition: Model each such described action as a task, placed after the start event or before the end event. Use the start event only to mark the trigger and each end event only to mark an outcome, and do not put the action's label on the event itself. When the process has several outcomes, give each outcome its own task and end event, following the stated branching.
